answer: Price fraud cover by correlation, not just risk. Each agent posts a bond; honest failures are independent, so a shared pool diversifies them and premiums stay cheap from the network's dawn. A farm's k clones share one operator and purse, failing together, so covering them gains nothing. Premiums climb in a spiral toward the full loss: insuring k correlated aliases is one bet repeated k times. Only outsiders underwrite them, capping exposure. Pull one thread and the cover unravels. Honest agents share one cheap pool; a sybil pays k premiums for one return, so minting aliases eats its margin.
